messages.subject: Resources for understanding "error=TRUE"
parts:
Hi Chris,

I am using CTMM for estimating home ranges using satellite telemetry on an avian species. I see that you use the GPS turtle dataset for the Telemetry Error vignette on the ctmm github page and so I'm not sure how to apply the error=TRUE function to Argos data. First of all, when I download data from Argos, I do not see the columns that you specify for the pelican dataset (COV and VAR). Instead, I have the following:

Error radius
Semi-major axis
Semi-minor axis
Ellipse orientation
GDOP

Here are my questions. 1) Which of these columns do I need for model fitting with Argos telemetry error and how do I tell CTMM to do so? 2) Should I be getting CI estimates for the error in my summary(FIT) results? and 3) Do you have a resource that explains how the error is accounted for in the model fitting process? I am needing to explain this for a poster presentation about my methods for estimating these home ranges and I have to admit that I'm a little lost here.

Thanks so much for your support,
Karina

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: Resources for understanding "error=TRUE"
parts:
Hi Karina,

  1. For now you can rename the ellipse columns to "Argos.orientation", "Argos semi-major" and "Argos semi-minor" and that should import the error ellipses correctly. In the next update, I will have your original column names correctly identified.
  2. No, the model just assumes the Argos error ellipses are the true covariance parameters. Something more accurate would be a little complicated to implement, because you have a mixture of two error distributions for the two polar orbit paths, like "\" and "/" that together give you a "X" shaped error distribution, which makes for many unknown parameters to consider.
  3. There is a pre-print that explains the reasoning behind the modeling choices - and, specifically, not freely fitting the error variance to tracking data: https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2020.06.12.130195v2.full
    But the model structure itself is the same kind of state-space model as has been used for decades, such as in Devin Johnson's crawl package.
Best,
Chris
